'''Martinus (Tinus) Tels''' (16 August 1926 in [[Rotterdam]] – 2 January 2008 in [[Veldhoven]]) was a Dutch [[physicist]] and [[chemical engineering|chemical engineer]]. He was a [[professor]] of chemical engineering, [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the department of chemical engineering and the ninth [[rector magnificus]] of the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]].<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie">{{Citation |last= Huiskamp |first= Joep |title= De kleine TU/e encyclopedie 1956-2006 |year= 2006 |location= Eindhoven |language= Dutch |isbn= 90-73192-30-7}}</ref><ref name="ED">{{cite news |title=Necrologie prof.ir. M. Tels, 1926-2008 |author=Patrick Wiercx |newspaper=[[Eindhovens Dagblad]] |date=4 January 2010 |language= Dutch}}</ref><ref name="Cursor">{{cite news |title=In memoriam |author=Ir. H.P.J.M. Roumen |newspaper=Cursor (TU/e University newspaper) |date=January 10, 2010 |url=http://web.tue.nl/cursor/internet/jaargang50/cursor16/nieuws/index.php?page=n_kb3 |language= Dutch|accessdate=27 September 2010}}</ref>

==Biography==
Martinus Tels was born on 16 August 1926 in [[Rotterdam]]. He was the son of [[Harry Hijman Tels]] (a lawyer) and Lucie Juliette Elias.<ref name="AKEVOTH">{{Cite web |url=http://stenenarchief.nl/genealogie/gezin/hum_duparc/F5892/I13796/ |title=Family trees |work=Family tree service |publisher=AKEVOTH |accessdate=27 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724165650/http://stenenarchief.nl/genealogie/gezin/hum_duparc/F5892/I13796/ |archivedate=24 July 2011 }}</ref> The Tels family was a reasonably prominent Jewish family in The Netherlands (in addition to Harry Hijman being a lawyer, Harry's grandfather [[Hartog Hijman Tels]] was the first editor of the [[NRC Handelsblad]]), as was the Elias family (the Elias family owned a large textile factory); because of this the family was added to the [[Plan Frederiks|Barneveld group]] during [[World War II]]. As part of this group, Martinus Tels was interned in [[Barneveld (town)|Barneveld]], then in the [[Westerbork transit camp]] and finally in the [[Theresienstadt concentration camp]].<ref name="Barneveldgroep">{{Cite web |url=http://www.joodsmonument.nl/page/274210 |title=Barneveldgroep |work=JoodsMonument |publisher=Joods Historisch Museum |accessdate=27 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110419151041/http://www.joodsmonument.nl/page/274210 |archivedate=19 April 2011 }}</ref><ref name="EenGelukkigeTijd">{{cite video | people = Paul Cohen (director), Oeke Hoogendijk (writer, director) | date = 20 May 1998 | title = Een gelukkige tijd - het verhaal van de Barneveldjoden | url = https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0164033/ | medium  = Television production | language = Dutch | publisher = NPS | location = Netherlands | accessdate  = 28 September 2010}}</ref> Surviving the war, he returned to The Netherlands by way of [[Switzerland]] in 1945.

Arriving back in The Netherlands he completed his secondary education and then attended the [[Delft University of Technology]] to study [[chemistry]].<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie"/> He stayed on at Delft as an [[associate professor]] (then called a ''hoofdassistent'' in Dutch), doing research in mixing solid oils with sugars and the purification of [[surface water]].<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie"/> During these years he also worked for [[zionist]] causes and was president of the {{Interlanguage link multi|Dutch Zionist Union|nl|3=Nederlandse Zionistenbond}} (Dutch: ''Nederlandse Zionistenbond'').<ref name="ED"/>

In 1960 he moved to [[Caltex]], to become head of the [[distillation]] lab. He was with Caltex until 1969 and in that time also headed the pilot plants division and finally the division for ''"[[applied mathematics]] and electronic [[data processing]]"''. In 1967 he was also appointed [[professor|extraordinary professor]] of Physical Technology (now called Chemical Engineering) at the [[University of Amsterdam]]; here he researched drag-reduction, the mixing of liquids in packed beds and thermal stability of [[Adiabatic process|adiabatic]] [[Continuous stirred-tank reactor|stirred reactors]].<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie"/>

Professor Tels was appointed full professor of physical technology at the department of Chemical Engineering of the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] in 1974. In this position he researched the uses of [[pyrolysis]] in physical technology and in the separation of solid [[Waste|waste materials]].<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie"/><ref name="ED"/><ref>{{Cite journal| last1 = Senden | first1 = M.| last2 = Tels | first2 = M.| title = Combination and/or Integration of Unit Operations in Dry Municipal Waste Processes| journal = Chemie Ingenieur Technik| volume = 51| issue = 2| pages = 132| year = 1979| doi = 10.1002/cite.330510216}}</ref> His expertise brought him into contact with the Van Gansewinkel waste management company, which he advised for years. He was one of the first researchers in The Netherlands working on waste management; for this reason he was jokingly called "the garbage professor".<ref name="ED"/>

[[File:Prof Tels bij protestactie ESVB 1988 (2).JPG|left|thumb|Professor Tels, joining a student protest against minister Deetman of Education in 1988.<br/>''Courtesy of [[Eindhoven University of Technology|Eindhoven University of Technology archives]]''.]]

Aside from his research, Tels had a reputation for being a good teacher and employing (often self-deprecating) humor in order to engage his students.<ref name="Cursor"/> He was appointed vice dean of the department in 1977 and became dean in 1982.<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie"/><ref name="Cursor"/>

Tels was appointed [[rector magnificus]] of the university in 1988. In his period as rector he focused on strengthening ties with the city of [[Eindhoven]] and with local industry.<ref name="Cursor"/> He was asked to resign as rector by the university council in 1991, following the [[Henk Buck|Buck-Goudsmit scandal]].<ref name="KleineEncyclopedie"/><ref name="ED"/><ref name="Cursor"/> Although he was finally not forced out, he resigned as rector to prevent an administrative crisis at the university.<ref name="Cursor"/>

Upon his resignation he was awarded the Honors Medal of the university by the TU/e, which he received from his successor as rector [[Jack van Lint|Professor Van Lint]].<ref name="Cursor"/> The year after his retirement from the university he was made a [[Order of the Netherlands Lion|Knight in the Order of the Dutch Lion]], after being nominated jointly by the [[Ministry of Education, Culture and Science (Netherlands)|Minister of Education]] for his work as a professor and by the [[Ministry of Housing, Spatial Planning and the Environment|Minister of the Environment]] for his work in environmental technology.<ref name="ED"/><ref name="Cursor"/>

Professor Tels continued advising the Van Gansewinkel Group until 1996, through Swiwah B.V., a one-man company he founded (''swiwah'' is [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] for "environment"). He died on 2 January 2008, after suffering a [[heart attack]].<ref name="Cursor"/>
{{Clear}}

==Honors==
During his career, professor Tels received the following honors:
* Lenin medal of the University of Sofia (1983?)
* Honors Medal of the Eindhoven University of Technology (1991)
* Knight in the Order of the Dutch Lion (1992)
